executive_summary: Markets are navigating a knife-edge as the US-Iran ceasefire expires tomorrow with no confirmed second round of talks — Iran re-closed the Strait of Hormuz after the US seized a cargo vessel, sending Brent crude surging 5.6% to $95.42 and collapsing strait traffic to just 16 ships on Monday. Futures are modestly green (S&P +0.19%, Nasdaq +0.20%) on hopes that Apple's orderly CEO succession to John Ternus and Kevin Warsh's dovish Fed confirmation testimony will stabilize sentiment. Earnings from GE Aerospace and AT&T provide company-specific catalysts, while gold holds below $4,800 and the dollar strengthens to 98.3 on safe-haven demand. The dominant risk is binary: if the ceasefire lapses without a deal, expect Brent above $100 and a hard risk-off rotation into defense, energy, and tankers at the expense of airlines, consumer discretionary, and EM currencies.

macro_events.title: US-Iran Ceasefire Expiry & Strait of Hormuz Blockade
macro_events.causal_chain: US naval blockade of Hormuz + Iran re-closure → only 16 ships transited Monday vs normal 60-80/day → 21% of global oil and 20% of LNG passes through strait → Brent surges to $95.42 (+5.6%) → war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs → Asian refiners forced to reroute via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M per trip) → Qatar LNG to Europe at risk → Dutch TTF gas futures elevated → global inflation expectations rise → central banks constrained from cutting → risk-off rotation into commodities and defense
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Global — direct impact on Middle East, Asia-Pacific (Japan, Korea, India as major oil importers), Europe (LNG dependency), US (inflation pass-through)
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent +15% in 24 hours, tanker rates surged 20-35% in one week, then normalized within 3 weeks as Saudi restored production. Current crisis is more sustained given active naval blockade vs one-off attack.
macro_events.counterargument: US CENTCOM clarified blockade targets only Iranian-port traffic, not general transit. If ceasefire extends or a deal materializes in Islamabad talks, oil could retrace 10%+ rapidly as it did last Friday when Hormuz briefly reopened.

macro_events.title: Kevin Warsh Fed Chair Confirmation Hearing
macro_events.causal_chain: Warsh testifies at 10 AM before Senate Banking Committee → prepared remarks signal firm inflation commitment but also AI-as-disinflation thesis → markets parse every word on independence from Trump pressure → if perceived as dovish, rate-cut expectations advance → 2Y yield falls, growth/tech outperforms → if hawkish on inflation (oil shock concern), yields rise and duration sells off → Tillis blocking vote adds uncertainty — confirmation may stall → Powell stays longer, reducing policy pivot probability
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-centric but global implications for dollar, EM debt, and carry trades
macro_events.historical_analog: Bernanke 2005 confirmation — markets initially sold off on uncertainty, then rallied once dovish continuity was confirmed. Key difference: Warsh faces active oil shock that constrains dovish pivot.
macro_events.counterargument: Tillis block may delay confirmation indefinitely, making this hearing more theater than substance. Markets may look through the hearing to FOMC on Apr 28-29.

affected_tickers.reason: Bond ETF sensitive to any rate guidance signals at $87.05
Tech/growth benefits if Warsh signals dovish tilt
Broad market awaits clarity on Fed direction

macro_events.title: Apple CEO Succession — Cook to Chairman, Ternus to CEO
macro_events.time_horizon: Multi-month transition through Sep 1 effective date
macro_events.causal_chain: Tim Cook announces transition to Executive Chairman → John Ternus (hardware engineering SVP) named CEO effective Sep 1 → market initially sells AAPL on uncertainty → Ternus is hardware-first leader (iPad, iPhone, Apple Silicon) → signals potential pivot toward product innovation over services margin optimization → supply chain and product roadmap continuity maintained → long-term neutral to positive if Vision Pro and AI hardware accelerate under Ternus
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Global — Apple $3T+ market cap impacts every major index, supply chain spans US, China, India, Vietnam
macro_events.historical_analog: Steve Jobs to Tim Cook transition (Aug 2011) — AAPL dropped 0.7% on announcement day, then rallied 25% over next 6 months as operational continuity was confirmed.
macro_events.counterargument: Cook remaining as Chairman ensures continuity. Ternus is deeply embedded — this is the most orderly Big Tech succession in a decade. Market may quickly price in continuity premium.

affected_tickers.reason: Apple largest chip supplier — Ternus hardware focus could mean accelerated orders
Modem supplier relationship may shift under hardware-focused CEO

macro_events.title: China Export Slump — March Data Misses Badly
macro_events.causal_chain: China March exports +2.5% vs +8.6% expected → Middle East conflict disrupting global shipping demand → exports to US down 26.5% YoY reflecting ~30% effective tariff rate → but imports surged 27.8% (strongest since Nov 2021) suggesting domestic stimulus gaining traction → weak exports pressure CNH → PBOC may ease further → cheaper Chinese goods compete with EM manufacturers
macro_events.historical_analog: 2019 trade war export slump — China exports fell 1.3% in May 2019, PBOC responded with targeted RRR cuts, Shanghai Composite bottomed within 6 weeks.
macro_events.counterargument: Import surge suggests domestic demand is healthy — this may be Hormuz-driven shipping disruption rather than structural demand weakness. Tariff extension through Nov 2026 provides some stability.

Domestic consumption strength offsets export weakness
